screening_decisions.reason: Prospective randomized clinical trial comparing biocompatible (polyacrylonitrile) vs bioincompatible (cuprophane) membranes in adult ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. Meets all PICO criteria.
Observational/historical review discussing hemodialysis complications and renal recovery. Not a randomized trial comparing membrane types.
Prospective observational study assessing prognostic factors in septic ARF. Although it mentions membrane type as a variable, it is not an RCT comparing BCM vs BICM.
Prospective randomized study comparing biocompatible (polyacrylonitrile) vs bioincompatible (cuprophane) membranes in ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing high-permeability vs conventional hemofiltration, both using synthetic membranes. Does not compare BCM vs BICM, and uses hemofiltration rather than intermittent hemodialysis.
Meta-analysis focusing on myocardial infarction treatments. Irrelevant population and intervention.
Compares two synthetic membranes (polyamide vs polyacrylonitrile) in intermittent hemofiltration. Does not compare BCM vs BICM, and modality is hemofiltration.

RCT comparing cellulose acetate (substituted cellulose) vs polysulfone (synthetic) membranes in ARF patients requiring intermittent hemodialysis. Directly addresses membrane comparison in the target population; warrants full-text review to confirm classification.
Meta-analysis of existing trials. Not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Methodological paper on statistical measures for meta-analyses. Irrelevant to the clinical question.
Clinical trial comparing biocompatible vs bioincompatible membranes in ARF patients requiring hemodialysis. Directly addresses the PICO and likely represents an RCT or quasi-RCT.
Observational prognostic study in acute tubular necrosis. No comparison of dialysis membranes.
Compares two synthetic membranes (PAN vs polysulfone) in continuous venovenous dialysis. Does not compare BCM vs BICM, and uses continuous rather than intermittent hemodialysis.
Review article summarizing published clinical trials. Not a primary study.
Commentary discussing discordant meta-analyses. Not a primary clinical trial.
Abstract text is garbled/mismatched, containing references to rat diets and OECD guidelines. Does not describe a relevant human RCT.
Study on publication bias in oncology trials. Irrelevant population and topic.
Review article on dialysate purity and inflammation. Not an RCT comparing membrane biocompatibility in ARF.
Evaluates pretransplantation hemodialysis strategy in kidney transplant recipients. Population is not ARF patients requiring intermittent HD for ARF.
Observational registry study analyzing risk factors for mortality in ICU ARF. No comparison of dialysis membranes.
This is a review article that summarizes existing clinical trials on dialysis-related variables. It is not a primary randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trial.

Quasi-randomized crossover study (alternate assignment) comparing cellulose acetate (substituted cellulose) vs polysulfone (synthetic biocompatible) membranes in 24 ARF patients requiring intermittent hemodialysis. While outcomes are cellular markers rather than clinical outcomes, the study design meets criteria for membrane comparison in ARF.

Prospective randomized trial comparing cellulose diacetate (modified cellulosic membrane) vs polysulfone (biocompatible synthetic) in 159 ARF patients requiring HD. Outcomes include survival and renal recovery. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article discussing the concept of dialysis membrane biocompatibility and summarizing existing studies. Not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Randomized trial comparing low-flux polysulfone vs high-flux polyacrylonitrile membranes. Both are synthetic biocompatible membranes - does not compare BCM vs BICM as required by selection criteria.
Observational study using USRDS data on chronic hemodialysis patients (dialysis for at least 1 year). Not a randomized trial and population is chronic dialysis, not ARF.

Prospective randomized multicentre trial comparing bioincompatible Cuprophan vs biocompatible polymethyl-methacrylate membranes in 180 ARF patients. Primary outcome is survival. Meets all selection criteria.
Meta-analysis of ACE inhibitor trials for nondiabetic renal disease. Wrong intervention (pharmacological, not dialysis membranes) and wrong population (not ARF requiring hemodialysis).
Review article examining developments in renal replacement therapies. Not a primary randomized controlled trial.
Compares extended daily dialysis vs continuous hemodialysis (dialysis modalities), not biocompatible vs bioincompatible membranes. Wrong comparison per selection criteria.

Prospective multicenter study with quasi-randomization (alternating order assignment) comparing biocompatible membranes (low complement activation) vs bioincompatible cellulosic membranes (high complement activation) in 153 ARF patients. Outcomes include survival and renal recovery. Meets all selection criteria.

Observational analysis from French Prospective Multicenter Study where 'criteria for hemodialysis and type of membrane were not defined by a uniform protocol, as the centers followed their usual practice.' Not randomized or quasi-randomized.

Randomized trial comparing high-permeability vs conventional haemofiltration using polyamide membranes (both biocompatible). Uses continuous veno-venous haemofiltration (CRRT), not intermittent hemodialysis. Does not compare BCM vs BICM.
Discussion/debate article inviting experts to discuss opinions on nephron injury in ARF. Not a randomized controlled trial.
